title: PC Won't Turn On
description: Systematic diagnostic steps when a desktop or laptop shows no signs of power, fan spin, or LED activity.

steps.title: Check wall outlet & surge protector
steps.description: Plug a lamp or phone charger into the wall outlet or surge strip to confirm power delivery.

steps.title: Verify power cable & PSU switch
steps.description: Ensure the power cord is firmly seated into the back of the PSU and the PSU toggle switch is set to '|' (ON).

steps.title: Disconnect external USB devices
steps.description: Unplug all external USB hubs, printers, external hard drives, and flash drives to eliminate shorts.

steps.title: Perform hard power reset (drain capacitors)
steps.description: Unplug power cable, hold down PC power button for 30 seconds to drain motherboard capacitors, reconnect power and try booting.

steps.title: Inspect motherboard power connectors
steps.description: Ensure 24-pin ATX and 4/8-pin EPS CPU power cables are completely clipped in.
steps.warning: Ensure PC is unplugged before touching internal components.

steps.title: Test front panel power switch / jump pins
steps.description: Bypass the chassis power button by gently bridging the two motherboard PWR_SW header pins with a flathead screwdriver.
steps.warning: Be careful not to bridge incorrect motherboard pins.

steps.title: Test Power Supply (Paperclip test)
steps.description: Disconnect PSU cables from motherboard and GPU. Jump green PS_ON pin to any black GND pin with a paperclip to test fan spin.
steps.warning: Only perform if experienced with ATX pinouts.

title: No Display (Black Screen)
description: PC powers on (fans spin, LEDs light up) but monitor shows 'No Signal' or stays completely black.

steps.title: Verify monitor power & input source
steps.description: Ensure monitor power light is on and manually select correct input channel (HDMI 1, DisplayPort, etc.).

steps.title: Check GPU vs Motherboard display output
steps.description: If the computer has a dedicated graphics card, the display cable MUST be plugged into the GPU, NOT the motherboard.

steps.title: Swap display cable & port
steps.description: Try an alternative HDMI or DisplayPort cable and try connecting to a different port on the GPU.

steps.title: Check Motherboard Diagnostic LEDs / Beep Codes
steps.description: Observe debug LEDs (CPU, DRAM, VGA, BOOT) on motherboard or listen for POST speaker beeps.

steps.title: Reseat RAM modules
steps.description: Remove RAM sticks, blow out dust from slots, and firmly reseat. Try booting with only one stick in the primary recommended slot.
steps.warning: Always unplug AC power before removing RAM.

steps.title: Reseat Dedicated GPU & PCIe power cables
steps.description: Remove and reseat the graphics card in the top PCIe x16 slot. Ensure PCIe power connectors are securely latched.

steps.title: Clear CMOS / Reset BIOS
steps.description: Unplug power, remove the CR2032 coin-cell battery for 5 minutes (or bridge CLR_CMOS jumper) to restore default BIOS settings.

title: Slow Computer & High Resource Usage
description: System sluggishness, freezing, 100% disk/CPU utilization, and delayed responsiveness.

steps.title: Check Task Manager for bottleneck processes
steps.description: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), sort by CPU, Memory, and Disk to identify runaway applications.

steps.title: Inspect Startup Applications
steps.description: Disable unnecessary high-impact startup apps in Task Manager > Startup tab.

steps.title: Check Storage Space & Drive Health
steps.description: Ensure C: drive has at least 15-20% free space for virtual memory paging and temporary files.

steps.title: Check CPU Temperatures & Thermal Throttling
steps.description: Monitor hardware temps. Clean dust filters, fans, and check if thermal paste needs replacement.

steps.title: Run System Integrity Checks (SFC & DISM)
steps.description: Run 'sfc /scannow' and 'DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' in Administrator command prompt.

steps.title: Scan for Malware and Crypto-miners
steps.description: Run an offline Windows Defender scan or secondary scanner to detect hidden background miner scripts.

title: Internet Not Working
description: Wired or wireless connection shows 'No Internet Access' or cannot reach websites.

steps.title: Verify physical connection / Wi-Fi status
steps.description: Check if ethernet cable has link lights on NIC and switch, or if Wi-Fi is connected with valid signal.

steps.title: Check IP Address (APIPA 169.254.x.x check)
steps.description: Run 'ipconfig'. If IP begins with 169.254.x.x, the device failed to obtain an address from DHCP.

steps.title: Ping Default Gateway
steps.description: Ping router IP (e.g., ping 192.168.1.1). If this fails, local network/cabling is the issue.

steps.title: Ping Public IP (8.8.8.8)
steps.description: Ping 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1. If this succeeds but websites fail, the issue is DNS.

steps.title: Flush DNS Cache & Reset Winsock
steps.description: Run 'ipconfig /flushdns', 'netsh winsock reset', and 'netsh int ip reset' as Administrator.
steps.warning: Requires system reboot after winsock reset.

steps.title: Power cycle Modem and Router
steps.description: Unplug ISP modem and Wi-Fi router for 60 seconds, reconnect modem first, then router.

title: Wi-Fi Problems & Drops
description: Frequent wireless disconnections, weak reception, or inability to authenticate.

steps.title: Forget and reconnect to network
steps.description: Delete saved Wi-Fi profile and re-enter WPA/WPA2/WPA3 passphrase.

steps.title: Toggle Airplane mode / Wi-Fi adapter
steps.description: Disable and re-enable Wi-Fi adapter in Network Connections (ncpa.cpl).

steps.title: Switch between 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands
steps.description: Connect to 5 GHz for higher speed/less interference, or 2.4 GHz for greater range through walls.

steps.title: Disable Wi-Fi Power Saving
steps.description: In Device Manager > Wi-Fi adapter properties > Power Management, uncheck 'Allow computer to turn off this device to save power'.

steps.title: Update or rollback wireless NIC drivers
steps.description: Install latest OEM drivers directly from manufacturer (Intel, Realtek, Qualcomm).

title: Printer Problems & Stuck Queue
description: Printer offline, jobs stuck in spooler queue, or documents not printing.

steps.title: Check printer physical state & error lights
steps.description: Ensure paper is loaded, toner/ink is installed, trays are closed, and no paper jams exist.

steps.title: Verify IP address & Ping printer
steps.description: Print configuration page from printer LCD to verify IP. Ping printer IP from PC.

steps.title: Restart Print Spooler service
steps.description: Stop 'spooler' service, delete all files inside 'C:\Windows\System32\spool\PRINTERS', and start spooler service.

steps.title: Uncheck 'Use Printer Offline'
steps.description: Open Printer queue > Printer menu > Ensure 'Use Printer Offline' and 'Pause Printing' are unchecked.

steps.title: Reinstall printer driver (Standard TCP/IP port)
steps.description: Remove device from Control Panel, add via TCP/IP address with manufacturer PCL6 or PostScript driver.

title: Windows Update & System Problems
description: Windows update failure codes, loop reboots, or corrupt system components.

steps.title: Run Windows Update Troubleshooter
steps.description: Settings > System > Troubleshoot > Other troubleshooters > Windows Update > Run.

steps.title: Reset SoftwareDistribution folder
steps.description: Stop 'wuauserv' and 'bits', rename 'C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution' to '.old', and restart services.

steps.title: Execute DISM & SFC health restore
steps.description: Run 'DISM.exe /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth' followed by 'sfc /scannow'.

steps.title: Reboot into Safe Mode with Networking
steps.description: Hold Shift while clicking Restart > Troubleshoot > Advanced Options > Startup Settings > Safe Mode.

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD)
description: System crashes with stop codes (CRITICAL_PROCESS_DIED, KERNEL_SECURITY_CHECK_FAILURE, etc.).

steps.title: Record Stop Code and BugCheck Module
steps.description: Note the exact stop code string and failing driver (.sys file) displayed on the screen.

steps.title: Analyze Minidump with BlueScreenView / WinDbg
steps.description: Inspect dump files located in 'C:\Windows\Minidump' to identify the specific third-party driver causing the crash.

steps.title: Roll back recent driver / Windows updates
steps.description: If crash started after a recent GPU or device driver update, roll back in Device Manager.

steps.title: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic / MemTest86
steps.description: Test RAM for bit flips or faulty sectors using 'mdsched.exe' or bootable MemTest86.

steps.title: Check SMART disk health
steps.description: Run CrystalDiskInfo or 'wmic diskdrive get status' to detect impending drive failure.

title: Application Won't Start
description: Application crashes immediately upon launch, throws DLL errors, or hangs silently.

steps.title: End zombie instances in Task Manager
steps.description: Check Details tab for frozen existing processes of the executable and End Task.

steps.title: Run as Administrator / Compatibility Mode
steps.description: Right click executable > Run as administrator. Test compatibility settings if older software.

steps.title: Install Visual C++ Redistributable packages
steps.description: Install VC++ 2015-2022 x86 and x64 runtimes to resolve missing MSVCP140.dll / VCRUNTIME140.dll errors.

steps.title: Check Windows Event Viewer
steps.description: Open 'eventvwr.msc' > Windows Logs > Application > look for Error events with event source 'Application Error'.

steps.title: Verify Antivirus / Windows Defender Exclusion
steps.description: Check antivirus protection history to see if the executable or a dependency was quarantined.

title: Disk & Storage Problems
description: Disk read errors, slow file transfers, clicking noises, or missing partitions.

steps.title: Check SMART Attributes
steps.description: Inspect Reallocated Sectors Count, Current Pending Sector Count, and Uncorrectable Sector Count.
steps.warning: If reallocated sectors are steadily climbing, back up all critical data immediately.

steps.title: Run Check Disk (chkdsk)
steps.description: Run 'chkdsk /f C:' to repair logical file system index errors.

steps.title: Check SATA / NVMe cable & seating
steps.description: Ensure SATA data and power cables are firmly plugged in. For M.2 drives, reseat the drive in the slot.

steps.title: Inspect Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc)
steps.description: Check if drive appears as Unallocated, RAW, or Offline.

title: Audio & Sound Problems
description: No sound output, crackling audio, microphone not detected, or wrong playback device.

steps.title: Verify Default Playback Device
steps.description: Right click speaker icon > Sound settings > Choose where to play sound (Headphones vs Speakers vs HDMI).

steps.title: Check physical audio jacks & volume toggles
steps.description: Ensure 3.5mm plug is in light green audio-out jack and inline headset volume wheel is turned up.

steps.title: Restart Windows Audio Service
steps.description: Restart 'Audiosrv' and 'AudioEndpointBuilder' services in services.msc.

steps.title: Disable Audio Enhancements
steps.description: In sound device properties > Advanced tab > uncheck 'Enable audio enhancements'.

steps.title: Reinstall Realtek / OEM High Definition Audio driver
steps.description: Uninstall audio device from Device Manager and scan for hardware changes.

title: USB Device Not Recognized
description: USB drive or peripheral fails to mount, disconnects intermittently, or shows code 43 in Device Manager.

steps.title: Test directly on Rear Motherboard Ports
steps.description: Bypass front chassis ports and USB hubs by connecting directly to rear I/O motherboard ports.

steps.title: Check Device Manager for yellow exclamation marks
steps.description: Look for Unknown Device or Code 43 under Universal Serial Bus controllers.

steps.title: Disable USB Selective Suspend
steps.description: Power Options > Change plan settings > Advanced power settings > USB settings > USB selective suspend setting > Disabled.

steps.title: Uninstall USB Root Hubs and reboot
steps.description: In Device Manager, uninstall USB Root Hub (USB 3.0) and restart PC to force Windows driver reload.

title: Local Network & File Sharing Problems
description: Cannot view or access shared network folders (SMB), printers, or local NAS devices.

steps.title: Verify Network Profile is set to Private
steps.description: In Windows Settings > Network & Internet > Ethernet/Wi-Fi > Network profile type must be set to 'Private', not 'Public'.

steps.title: Enable Network Discovery & File Sharing
steps.description: Control Panel > Network and Sharing Center > Advanced sharing settings > Turn on network discovery and file/printer sharing.

steps.title: Test SMB connectivity with IP Address
steps.description: Press Win+R and type '\\<Target_IP_Address>\ShareName' instead of computer name to bypass NetBIOS name issues.

steps.title: Verify SMB 1.0 or SMB 2/3 requirements
steps.description: If connecting to legacy NAS devices, verify if SMBv1 client feature is required or upgrade NAS firmware.
steps.warning: SMB 1.0 has known security vulnerabilities. Only enable on trusted isolated networks if strictly necessary.

steps.title: Check Windows Credential Manager
steps.description: Add Windows Credentials in Control Panel for target host with username format 'TARGET_PC\username'.
